lesson: Today, we work on one technique. It is the turn. The turn is the exact spot where the poem stops describing and starts telling you what it means. Before the turn, this poem stays on the body and the room. You get the weight of yourself in the bed and the feet find the floorboards, cool and honest. That is all physical. Then it opens out. Somewhere a door of the season has swung open. That line is the turn. After it, the poem names the point directly, small good things, and they're all yours to meet. It works because you spend the whole poem in one small morning. So when it widens, you feel the lift without being pushed. Try this. Describe a plain scene for most of the poem, then put your one line of meaning near the end. The second time, mark the season line and hear how everything after it changes. Here's the poem.
